_doc: Time of day (render/daylight.gd) and the air the light comes through (render/air.gd, render/shaders/sky_model.gdshaderinc). air: the clear atmosphere as exponential layers, values from Bruneton & Neyret 2008 and Hillaire 2020 (EGSR, 'A Scalable and Production Ready Sky and Atmosphere Rendering Technique', sec. 3): rayleigh_beta_per_m the scattering of air at sea level for 680, 550 and 440 nm taken as r, g, b, rayleigh_height_m its scale height; ozone_beta_per_m its absorption at the layer's peak, the layer a tent ozone_thickness_m wide in all (half that at its peak's value) round ozone_height_m; aerosol_height_m the aerosol's scale height (Hillaire's Mie layer); aerosol_g its Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry (Hillaire, 0.8); aerosol_albedo the single-scattering albedo of urban aerosol (0.9: Dubovik et al. 2002, J. Atmos. Sci. 59, Table 1, urban-industrial sites 0.90 to 0.98 at 440 nm, the low end for a dense city). visibility_km: the meteorological visibility of a clear day in a large city (the WMO's 'clear' begins at 20 km); the aerosol's extinction at the ground is what Koschmieder's 3.912 / V leaves after the air's own Rayleigh at 550 nm, and the same number is the haze's density over the distance. sun_top_klx: the solar illuminance over the atmosphere (128 klx, the extraterrestrial solar illuminance of Darula, Kittler & Gueymard 2005, Solar Energy 79), The light's unit, the illuminance a light of energy 1 gives, is tuning.json render.light_unit_lx. channel_nm: the wavelengths the r, g and b channels stand for (the Rayleigh betas', the moon's colour). ground_albedo: the land under the sky as the sky's lower half sees it, a city's mean albedo (0.12 to 0.15, Taha 1997, Energy and Buildings 25), linear. exposure 2.47: a sunlit level ground of 18 % albedo at the day hour (sun at 29 degrees: its light after the air 0.66, 0.56, 0.43 on a level of sin 29 deg plus the clear sky's level light 0.117, 0.126, 0.176, a white floor at 0.405 luminance) shows as AgX's middle grey, 0.18, the way an exposure meter places a grey card in sun; agx_white and agx_contrast the engine's own defaults for AgX (Environment.tonemap_agx_white, tonemap_agx_contrast: Blender's AgX curve). overcast_pass: the global light under a fully overcast sky as a share of the clear sky's, 1 - 0.75 (N/8)^3.4 at N = 8 oktas (Kasten & Czeplak 1980, Solar Energy 24): the CIE overcast sky's level light. overcast_sun, overcast_sky: how much of the sun the weather's overcast takes and how much of the sky it covers. flash_sky: a bolt's light over the sky, as a share of it. light_from: the sun's height (sine of elevation) below which the moon lights the town. low_height: the least height the sun's shadows are cast from. hours, sun and moon arc in degrees. moon: the full moon, the sun's light it sends being 10^(-0.4 (magnitude - sun_magnitude)) of the sun's (apparent magnitudes -12.74 and -26.74, Allen's Astrophysical Quantities, 4th ed.: 1/400 000, 0.26 lx over the air), its colour the sun's times the moon's reflectance, which rises with the wavelength by reflectance_slope_per_nm of its value at 550 nm (the moon's B-V of 0.92 against the sun's 0.65, Allen: 0.78 at 440 nm; Kieffer & Stone 2005, ROLO, the same slope to 700 nm); the night sky is that moon through the same air (render/shaders/sky_model.gdshaderinc), with the town's own light scattered by it. sky_glow: the town's light in its sky, zenith_mag_arcsec2 the clear zenith's brightness measured at the IAG observatory inside Sao Paulo (V 16.49 mag/arcsec^2: Volpe et al., Boletim da SAB 2024; RMxAC 60), a luminance mag_zero_cd_m2 x 10^(-0.4 m) (22.0 mag/arcsec^2 is 0.171 mcd/m^2, Falchi et al. 2016, Science Advances 2); the town's upward light is what makes that zenith through the air, coloured as the street lamps' light (materials.json lamp_glow glow_color); cloud_reflect the share of it an overcast deck sends back down, a stratus's albedo (0.6, Liou, An Introduction to Atmospheric Radiation, 2nd ed., Table 6.3): overcast city nights are several times brighter (Kyba et al. 2011, PLoS ONE 6). sky_gain carries a colour authored as the screen shows it into this game's light: the unlit signal lenses, the clouds' authored light. eye: the eye's adaptation (render/eye.gd): the picture is pre-exposed by Ward's contrast-based scale factor (Ward 1994, Graphics Gems IV, 'A contrast-based scalefactor for luminance display': ((1.219 + Lda^0.4) / (1.219 + Lwa^0.4))^2.5, Lda half of display_cd_m2, the sRGB reference display's 80 cd/m^2, IEC 61966-2-1) at the luminance the eye adapts to, a grey_card of 18 % under the light of the sky, the sun and the moon, plus the lit street's luminance street_cd_m2 while the lamps are on (EN 13201-2:2015, class M3, 1.0 cd/m^2), over the same at the day hour, so the day keeps its exposure and the night its darkness. rooms: a lit room's working plane, a home's (100 lx, the middle of the 50 to 150 lx of living rooms, IES RP-11) and an office's (500 lx, EN 12464-1:2021 Table 5.26, writing and reading). glow_intensity and glow_threshold: the camera's bloom by day and night alike. shadow_bias_m: the depth bias along the light in the first cascade, in metres, and shadow_normal_bias the offset along the normal, in texels. The engine (tag 4.7.2-stable, light_storage.cpp, renderer_scene_cull.cpp) takes bias / 100 x (2 radius + pancake) x blur x filter radius for each cascade, so the bias in metres holds for the first cascade and the others grow with theirs, the same in texels. shadow_pancake_m: the DirectionalLight3D default. shadow_past_look, shadow_first_past_look, shadow_first_share: the cascades after Engel, ShaderX5, modelling choices; shadow_first_least_m and shadow_view_least_dip: a street-level view, measured on a sign post. awake_by_hour: the share of people not asleep at each hour from midnight, 100 % less the Sleeping row of BLS American Time Use Survey Table A-3 (2007-11, https://www.bls.gov/tus/tables/a3_0711.pdf): the rooms lit at night. daylight_factor: the share of the unobstructed sky's level light a room seen through its glass takes by day, 2 %, the average daylight factor below which a room no longer looks daylit (CIBSE LG10, BS 8206-2): the sky's level light is rendered by render/sky_light_probe.gd, the direct sun is outside the factor's definition. outside_all_night: the outside lights left on all night.

grade._doc: Film grade of the picture on screen (render/film_grade.cpp), read in the display image: neutral, the picture as AgX gives it (a camera's own rendering adds no contrast or vibrance of its own over its tone curve); the table stays so a grade can be set.

vignette._doc: How the picture falls off to the corners (render/shaders/vignette.gdshader), a modelling choice, the 4.0's own look.

occlusion._doc: Screen-space occlusion of the high presets (render/shaders/occlusion.gdshader): the 4.0's GTAO, blended over the whole picture. Its radius 1 reached by a random share of 0.5 to 1 of it; a fixed set of slices takes the mean. Its distance exponent, thickness, scale and intensity, the values modelling choices.
